Yes. I found a few GTA/Toronto marketers with actual wedding/bridal work and published case-study evidence, rather than agencies that merely say they “serve weddings.”

My shortlist

Mondo Bridal Agency — strongest niche fit

Toronto-based boutique agency specifically focused on the wedding industry.

Their positioning is unusually specialized: wedding-industry marketing/media, rather than generic small-business marketing.

I’d put them high on the list if you want someone who already understands bridal vendors, couples, wedding publications and the wedding buying journey.

Caveat: I found evidence of their wedding specialization, but less compelling public numerical case-study evidence than the options below.

Tidal Media — strong GTA wedding-venue case study

Their Spice Factory case study is particularly relevant: a Toronto event venue targeting weddings, corporate events and private bookings.

They report 2× event inquiries, 78% social growth and 31% website-traffic growth, using web design, SEO, social, ads and email marketing. 
tidalmedia.ca

This is one of the better matches if you're looking for a conventional digital agency that can demonstrate measurable results in the wedding/event space.

Mavlers — very strong recent GTA venue case study

They published a detailed case study for an anonymized Vaughan/Richmond Hill/GTA wedding/event venue.

Reported results: +179% organic sessions, +148% organic leads, 234 → 446 page-one keywords, and AI-search visibility going from zero to 32 mentions. 
Mavlers Agency

Their work covered SEO, content, local SEO, Google Business Profile and AI-search optimization.

Best fit: a venue or wedding business where Google/SEO is a major acquisition channel.

Firas Digital — excellent bridal-services case study

They have a Toronto/GTA case study for a makeup artist serving the wedding market.

The case study reports $20,000 in revenue in 90 days, with $2,000/month ad spend, using conversion tracking, a booking landing page and locally targeted paid social. 
Firas Digital

This is particularly interesting if you're a bridal beauty, photography, planning or other appointment-based business, because the acquisition model is much closer to those businesses than an e-commerce case study.

Ishant Sharma / Hustle Marketers — actual bridal-shop case study

They published an Estelle Bridal case study in August 2026, explicitly connecting the named bridal shop with Ishant Sharma/Hustle Marketers' SEO and digital-marketing work. 
Hustle Marketers

This is one I'd investigate further because the client itself is a bridal shop, rather than merely an event venue.

One particularly interesting wildcard

Paloma Blanca / Mikaella Bridals case study by HCO is probably the most directly relevant bridal-brand case study I found. The agency says it consolidated the two bridal brands' websites and increased monthly visitors from 5,000 to 20,000—a 4× increase—with SEO designed to get brides discovering gowns and then visiting authorized retailers. 
H&CO

The question is whether you specifically need a GTA-based agency; if that's a hard requirement, I'd rank the options differently.

My ranking if you're hiring for a GTA wedding business

If you tell me what kind of wedding business you have (planner, photographer, venue, bridal boutique, DJ, makeup artist, decor, etc.) and roughly what you want to spend per month, I can narrow this to 3 GTA marketers and compare their actual case studies, services, pricing signals, reviews, and contact links.
